stories.title: Sparkle and the Picture With No Applause
stories.outro: See you next time in Sunny Meadow!
stories.moral: You can enjoy what you make even without a round of applause.
moralRhyme: Draw the thing you like to see,
Your own joy can simply be!

youtube.title: Sparkle and the Picture With No Applause | Sunny Meadow
youtube.description: Sparkle waited for applause that never came. Ozzy was still reading the last page of his book. A gentle friendship story. You can enjoy what you make even without a round of applause. #SunnyMeadow #DreamyDiscoveries

lines.text: Sparkle waited for applause that never came.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ozzy was still reading the last page of his book.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ta-da! My new rainbow has seven enormous stripes!
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I have one page left. May I look when I finish?
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle wanted her picture to feel worth making.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The silent moment made her rainbow seem smaller.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I thought you would clap as soon as you saw it.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I have not had a chance to look at it properly.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle added a giant gold star beside the rainbow.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She held the page up higher than before.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Perhaps this star will make the picture exciting enough.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Your picture can wait beside me while I finish reading.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle tried announcing it in a grand performer voice.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ozzy kept his bookmark ready beside the little chair.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Presenting the most tremendous rainbow in Sunny Meadow!
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I heard you. I still need a moment with my book.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Does silence mean Sparkle's picture is bad?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Sparkle lowered her page and stared at the new star.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She could not remember wanting it there before.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I put that star in because nobody clapped.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: What did you enjoy drawing before you hoped for applause?
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle looked at the long blue stripe near the middle.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It curved more gently than all the other colors.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I liked making that blue part bend like a river.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You can keep enjoying that part while I finish here.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle sat beside her crayons instead of announcing again.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She traced the curve in the air above her page.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I also like where the purple meets the blue.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Those sound like things you noticed for yourself.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle decided to add a tiny boat under the rainbow.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She chose it because the blue curve suggested water.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: My little river could have somewhere for a boat.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Then make the part your own idea wants to see.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle drew a boat with one small triangular sail.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Her page became interesting before anyone said a word.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I like how the sail fits inside this space.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: She moved the crayon carefully along the boat's little side.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Can Sparkle decide what she likes in her picture?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ozzy finished his book and placed the bookmark inside.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He turned toward Sparkle without making a big announcement.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Would you like me to show you the boat?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Yes. I have time to look at your picture now.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle described the blue curve and tiny sail.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ozzy listened before pointing to the little boat.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: That is my favorite part because it started a new idea.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I can see how the rainbow gave your river its shape.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Ozzy thanked Sparkle for showing him her work.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: There was no great cheering sound around the quiet table.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I thought I needed clapping to know I liked it.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You had already found several parts you enjoyed.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle set her drawing where she could see it later.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She put the gold crayon back beside the others.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The star can stay. I like its little crooked corner.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Your boat seems to have an excellent view of it.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Sparkle gave her tiny painted boat a solemn inspection.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ozzy picked up his bookmark with a smile.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: One problem. My passenger forgot to bring a sandwich.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Then your next drawing may require a very small picnic.
lines.speaker: friend
